description: A bounded catalog of curated shareable records for an offline hackathon advisor.
mode: Saved lessons + deterministic matching; no live model or Cognee query.

lessons.title: Try a short commitment together.
lessons.lesson: A short invitation can be worth trying when someone is unsure whether to stay and build.
lessons.what_happened: John reported being ready to leave because information about how and where to use the products was unclear. Rene suggested a short trial together. They chose another 15 minutes, then a two-hour project target. John remembers enjoying building together.
lessons.why: The account suggests that a small commitment and another person made continuing appealing. That is an interpretation, not an established cause. No measured speedup, actual build duration or comparison with working alone is recorded.
lessons.reuse_when: When a potential teammate is interested but unsure about committing, offer a brief trial with a clear stopping point.
lessons.rule_to_challenge: “Always make only a short commitment.” A team with a clear shared goal might benefit from agreeing on a longer working block.
lessons.experiment: Propose a 15-minute trial together, then explicitly choose whether to stop, continue or change direction. If the team already has a shared goal, compare that choice with a longer planned block.
lessons.hypothesis: A small, reversible invitation may help people decide whether they want to collaborate.
lessons.observable_check: At the agreed checkpoint, ask each person whether the goal became clearer, whether they want to continue and what they actually completed. Record elapsed time separately from the target.
lessons.disconfirming_result: If people feel pressured, the goal stays unclear, or no one wants to continue, do not promote the short-trial idea into a rule.

lessons.title: Choose the smallest slice that answers the question.
lessons.lesson: Choose one actor, problem and outcome. Build the smallest runnable slice, check observable behavior, save the result, then repeat, recover or cut.
lessons.what_happened: No recorded comparative outcome accompanies this saved method. It does not show that a smaller build was faster, won a prize or worked better at a particular event.
lessons.why: The proposed rationale is to get evidence before adding more work. That rationale is not a measured result.
lessons.reuse_when: When you can learn something useful from one runnable path and you have a clear acceptance check.
lessons.rule_to_challenge: “Always make the scope smaller.” If the uncertainty is in integration between two parts, a broader end-to-end slice may be the smallest meaningful test.
lessons.experiment: Name the decision the prototype must resolve. Choose either one isolated component or one connected path, depending on where the uncertainty sits. Set a time cap and a pass/fail observation before building.
lessons.hypothesis: The chosen slice can resolve the stated uncertainty within the agreed budget.
lessons.observable_check: Run the acceptance check on the artifact. Record what it demonstrates, what remains unknown, the elapsed time and the next decision it changes.
lessons.disconfirming_result: If the slice passes but leaves the original decision unresolved, it was too narrow or tested the wrong thing.

lessons.title: Keep the claim no stronger than its evidence.
lessons.lesson: Separate verified facts, observations, interpretations, proposals and unknowns. A claim that something is working needs execution evidence tied to its exact scope.
lessons.what_happened: No recorded outcome in this method proves that evidence labels improved judging, team understanding or build quality.
lessons.why: Labels help a reader see what is supported and what still needs a check. Whether they improve a particular decision remains something to test.
lessons.reuse_when: When preparing a demo, evaluating a sponsor integration or deciding whether a result is strong enough to rely on.
lessons.rule_to_challenge: “Show every piece of evidence on the first screen.” A short decision summary with accessible supporting detail may be easier to understand; keep the important uncertainty visible.
lessons.experiment: Take one claim and label it as an observation, method, proposal or unknown. Show the supporting artifact and the check needed to strengthen it. Try a concise summary with the evidence one step away.
lessons.hypothesis: A concise, correctly labeled claim can stay understandable without hiding its limitations.
lessons.observable_check: Ask an uncoached viewer to explain what actually ran, what was merely proposed and what remains unknown. Record any mistaken inference.
lessons.disconfirming_result: If the viewer believes a mockup is a live integration or a proposal is an observed result, the explanation has not passed.

lessons.title: Inspect the evidence behind a plausible tally.
lessons.lesson: When output and field evidence disagree, open the actual material and examine what the pipeline was looking for.
lessons.what_happened: The public post-event review reports zero confirmed locate marks from the video pass. A later human review identified 26 photos containing real locate paint. These are different units, not an accuracy score. The detector’s most common color was orange; the photographed markings were mostly red and green.
lessons.why: The color mismatch is a lead to investigate, not a demonstrated cause. The record does not establish how much of the disagreement came from color assumptions, different source material or other factors.
lessons.reuse_when: When a believable count conflicts with examples you can inspect, or when a pipeline result looks complete but may be answering the wrong question.
lessons.rule_to_challenge: “Trust the aggregate tally once the pipeline finishes.” Inspect a known example and test the assumptions before relying on the total.
lessons.experiment: Use a known marked block and a fixed set of images. Review the color assumptions, then compare the original and revised detector against the same labeled material. Keep measured photo EXIF positions distinct from reconstructed video positions; neither is survey-grade.
lessons.hypothesis: Revised color assumptions may improve detection on the same labeled material. The earlier review does not prove this hypothesis.
lessons.observable_check: For both runs, record detected and missed markings against the same human-reviewed units. Inspect example frames and report position provenance separately.
lessons.disconfirming_result: If changing color assumptions does not improve the fixed-set result, or only changes the count without locating the known marks, investigate another cause.
